docRequirement: worktrees.md:134-146 binds us to a `.worktreeinclude` file at the PROJECT root: "To copy them automatically when Claude creates a worktree, add a `.worktreeinclude` file to your project root." It "uses `.gitignore` syntax. Only files that match a pattern and are also gitignored are copied, so tracked files are never duplicated" (:136), and it "applies to every worktree Claude Code creates with git: `--worktree` worktrees, subagent worktrees, and parallel sessions in the desktop app" (:146). One carve-out: with a `WorktreeCreate` hook, "`.worktreeinclude` is not processed" and the hook script copies instead (:146, :215).
current: No reader exists anywhere. `grep -rain worktreeinclude --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.json' --include='*.js' packages apps scripts` returns zero hits (positive control on the same rig: `sparsePaths` → 49 hits). The whole creation path is: `WorktreeLeaseService.acquireUnlocked` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:207-234) selects a path, fires `WorktreeCreate` via `applyWorktreeCreateHookPath` (:251-284), then calls `this.options.git.create(lease)` (:227). The single production implementation of `git.create` is packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10164-10198: it runs `show-ref` for branch existence, then every command from `worktreeCreateCommands` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96 — `worktree add`, optional `sparse-checkout set --cone`, `checkout`, and nothing else), then the links from `worktreeSymlinkPlan` (worktree-git-plan.ts:112-124 — `settings.symlinkDirectories` only). There is no file copy of any kind on the path. Both entry points converge here: `EnterWorktree` (SessionManager.ts:10269, handler at packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts:19-43) and subagent `isolation: worktree` (SessionManager.ts:10334-10347) both call `service.acquire`. Nor is there a settings-level escape: packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:60,78-83 admits exactly `baseRef`/`symlinkDirectories`/`sparsePaths`/`bgIsolation` and THROWS `invalid worktree setting: <key>` on anything else, with both list defaults empty (:71-76).
divergence: The entire mechanism is missing — not a wrong key name, not a narrower match. Nothing ever opens `<projectRoot>/.worktreeinclude`, nothing parses gitignore syntax for it, and no file is copied into a worktree. The two adjacent things we DO ship are not it: (a) `symlinkDirectories` symlinks rather than copies, takes a plain repo-relative path list rather than gitignore syntax, defaults empty, and has no "and is also gitignored" filter — an entry pointing at a file does work today (SessionManager.ts:10190 only checks `existsSync`), so it is a partial user-side workaround with different semantics (writes inside the worktree write through to the main checkout, and realpath-resolving tools see the main repo); (b) the `WorktreeCreate` hook we ship (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:360,1247-1259) is precisely the alternative the page names INSTEAD of `.worktreeinclude`, not an implementation of it. Second-order: our `WorktreeCreate` hook replaces only the PATH (worktree-lease-service.ts:251-284) and `git.create` still runs afterwards, so the doc's "hook is used ⇒ do not process `.worktreeinclude`" carve-out has no existing flag to hang off.

change.what: New pure planner, sibling to worktree-git-plan.ts and following the same 'assertable without a repository' shape. (1) `parseWorktreeInclude(text: string): WorktreeIncludePattern[]` — gitignore syntax: drop blank lines and `#` comments (`\#` escapes), trim unescaped trailing whitespace, record `negated` for a leading `!`, `anchored` for a leading `/`, `directoryOnly` for a trailing `/`. Cap entries (reuse the 128/512 limits from worktree-settings.ts) and refuse `..` segments and absolute forms exactly as `repoRelativePaths` does — a `.worktreeinclude` must not be able to name a file outside the repo. (2) `worktreeIncludeCandidateCommands(repoRoot)` → the `WorktreeGitCommand`s that produce the authoritative candidate set: `['-C', repoRoot, 'ls-files', '-z', '--others', '--ignored', '--exclude-standard', '--directory', '--no-empty-directory']` (operation `include-list`, cwd `repo`, `allowFailure: true`) — `--directory --no-empty-directory` is what keeps a repo with `node_modules` from emitting 200k paths — plus, for every wildcard-free pattern, a targeted `['-C', repoRoot, 'check-ignore', '-q', '--', <pattern>]` so a file inside a wholly-collapsed ignored directory is still reachable. Using git as the ignore engine is what satisfies 'also gitignored' without a second ignore implementation. (3) `worktreeIncludePlan({ repoRoot, worktreePath, patterns, ignoredEntries })` → `{ source, destination }[]`, applying LAST-matching-pattern-wins with negation (gitignore's rule, which `matchGitignoreGlob` does not implement) and joining against the resolved roots so a destination can only land inside the worktree.

After the `worktreeCreateCommands` loop (so a sparse checkout has materialised) and alongside the existing symlink loop, add the include step: read `<root>/.worktreeinclude` (root = `(await worktreeAuthority()).root`, the PROJECT root, i.e. the same path `projectRoot()` returns — NOT the worktree and NOT `.nessy-agent/`; the filename carries no brand so it is not renamed by the de-brand). Absent file ⇒ no-op. Run the candidate commands through the existing `runGit` (its `profile: 'read-only'` + `additionalWritableRoots: [root, namespaceRoot]` already covers this), feed the output to `worktreeIncludePlan`, then for each pair `mkdir(dirname(destination), { recursive: true })` and `copyFile(source, destination)` with `chmod` to the source's mode (these are secrets — `.env` at 0600 must not land 0644), skipping when the destination already exists. Failure tolerance must match the symlink precedent immediately below (`sessionLog.warn`, never fail creation) — including a malformed `.worktreeinclude`. Skip-if-exists is load-bearing beyond politeness: `WorktreeLeaseService.recoverUnlocked` re-invokes `git.create` for a `creating` lease (worktree-lease-service.ts:296), so the step must be idempotent.

One-line-ish plumbing for the :215 carve-out. Have `applyWorktreeCreateHookPath` report whether it adopted a hook-returned path, and widen `create(lease: WorktreeLeaseV1)` to `create(lease: WorktreeLeaseV1, context: { hookReplacedPath: boolean })`; `SessionManager`'s implementation skips the include step when it is true. Pass it as a call argument, NOT as a field on `WorktreeLeaseV1` — that type is persisted (`managed.worktreeLeaseState`, schemaVersion 1) and adding a field there turns an M into a persistence-boundary change for no gain. `recoverUnlocked`'s `git.create` call (:296) passes `{ hookReplacedPath: false }`.

Table-driven over the parser and the plan, no repository needed: the doc's own three-line example (`.env`, `.env.local`, `config/secrets.json`) copies exactly those three; a negation (`.env*` then `!.env.production`) excludes the last; a tracked file that matches a pattern but is absent from the ignored-entries set is NOT copied; `..`, an absolute entry and a comment line are refused/ignored; and a pattern matching an entry collapsed to `node_modules/` does not expand into the directory. Extend packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.test.ts only if the candidate commands land in that module instead.

Explicit non-change. It is tempting to extend it for `!`/leading-`/`/trailing-`/`, but it is the permission matcher: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/permission-dsl.ts:6 imports it and its semantics are pinned to permissions.md's documented subset (module header, :1-10). Reuse it read-only for the glob core inside the new planner and keep the gitignore-only rules local. Likewise do not add a key to packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts — `.worktreeinclude` is a project-root file, not a settings key, and that parser throws on unknown keys by design.

blastRadius: Confined to packages/server-core plus one read-only import from packages/shared. Readers of the touched symbols: `git.create` has exactly one production implementation (SessionManager.ts:10164) and two call sites inside WorktreeLeaseService (:227 acquire, :296 recover); widening its signature touches packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.test.ts and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-orphan-sweep.test.ts, which build fake `git` ports. `worktreeSymlinkPlan` has 3 callers in SessionManager.ts and is covered by packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.test.ts. Both product entry points inherit the fix for free — `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts) via SessionManager.ts:10269, and subagent `isolation: worktree` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:47,109,417) via SessionManager.ts:10345 — so there is one fix point, not three. NO wire or schema boundary is crossed IF the hook flag rides the call argument; putting it on `WorktreeLeaseV1` would cross the persisted `worktreeLeaseState` boundary (schemaVersion 1) and is explicitly rejected above. There IS a security boundary: this is the first code path that copies gitignored secrets out of the main checkout into `<dirname(repo)>/.nessy-worktrees/<slug>/<leaseId>/`, a directory that outlives the session until the `cleanupPeriodDays` sweep (packages/shared/src/sessions/worktree-orphans.ts) removes it, and a subagent running under `isolation: worktree` is exactly the actor that was previously denied those files. Mode preservation and containment of the destination path are the two things review must check.
userImpact: Observable today. A user whose project keeps local config in a gitignored `.env` runs a subagent with `isolation: worktree`, or the model calls `EnterWorktree`, and the worktree comes up without it: `bun run dev`, a test suite, a migration or any script reading `.env` fails inside the worktree with missing-variable errors while the identical command works in the main checkout. The failure is opaque from the transcript — nothing says the file was not carried over — and the documented fix does not work, because writing `.worktreeinclude` at the project root has no effect and adding an equivalent settings key is rejected outright with `invalid worktree setting` (packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:81). Partial workarounds exist but are undiscoverable and differ in semantics: listing the file under `worktree.symlinkDirectories` produces a symlink rather than a copy (edits write through to the main checkout), or the user hand-writes a `WorktreeCreate` command hook.
